Reviews: I knew I wanted a phone with a large screen (5'"and up), but I didn't want to sacrifice portability. After looking through the galaxy note line, the 5"+ HTC phones, and the Huwei models I came to the conclusion that the LG G Optimus Pro was the optimal choice. (see what I did there?)BUILD With the exception of the Notes 3/4, the G Pro has the highest ratio of screen to front panel of any phablet. At 5.91 x 3.00 x 0.37 inches, the G Pro is only marginally larger than the HTC One M8 (5.76 x 2.78 x 0.37 inches) but manages to pack an additional 1/2 inch of screen. The LG G Pro fits well in the majority of my pockets and doesn't limit my range motion any. As for materials, its plastic. It feels like a Happy Meal toy and suffers the same cheap feeling of any other plastic phone. Fortunately, the side of the phone features a metal rim that makes it feel a little more substantial.One of the big things I look for in a phone is a removable battery. It a necessity in the Arizona valley, as the functional lifespan of any battery here is approximately "til' summer." Not only does the G Pro come with a removable battery, but comes with plenty of accessories like charging docks and extended batteries.PERFORMANCEWith a 1.7 Ghz quad core processor with 2gb ram, the G Pro is stupidly powerful. I can edit multiple word documents simultaneously without and lag and I've yet to find a game on the play store it couldn't handle. Despite its age, it holds up very well in terms of power. The IPS-LCD screen is phenomenal; it easily out shines the typical amoled/lcd displays I'd grown accustomed to over the years. The colors are bright and distinct and the 400+ ppi makes textures look smooth and refined. Unfortunately, all of this power comes with a price: battery life.At 40% brightness the phone probably puts up about 6 hours of screen time, but this number plummets if when you load a game or run a program script. Under moderate usage with battery conserving settings the phone lasted me through a typical day on a single charge (it has efficient standby conservation). Heavy users will definitely want to purchase a backup or extended battery for this phone.PRICINGThis phone floats are internet new for between $320-$400. I purchased a refurbished one here for $215 from the merchant: phonesforselling.I would recommend this seller whole heartily; my phone arrived in 3 days, coming with a case, charger, and screen wrap. The device was wiped, fully functional, and in pristine condition.CONCLUSIONIt works well for me. For anyone who's strapped for cash and looking for a premium phone experience, you'll be hard pressed to find a better deal than this.

Reviews: I've had this phone for 2 months.The Phone:Solid phone. Its great because its not pushing any technology envelope, its really reliable and consistent. I don't really want my phone to dominate my pockets... The screen size works very well. I watch netflix on it regularly, email, web pages load really well and are easy to navigate, games are good. Texting is easy. I like the swype. Its improved smooth and quick.And at $200 I'm not so worried about it. Can you imagine carrying a $400 object in your pocket! I'd think about it all the time. This is way lower stress and a gain in workability.+Music player works great. Good sound without any enhancements.+I like how they do the calendar and the day's appointments are displayed below the monthly calendar.+Contacts software is well integrated and usable.+Being able to create folders inside the app menu is nice.-I liked the text msgr until I realized it cut photos sent thru MMS down to 9kb, can't even see them. So I use GO Messaging from App market. It only cuts them down to 30kb. Which is very readable. (I didn't like Handcent because when monitoring memory usage with the apps open, Handcent took up more memory and left more memory tied up even after I closed it.)+It has Tasklist and Memo apps that are well thought out.+The pull-down bar lets you change screen orientation, wifi on/off, bluetooth settings. Very handy.+Photo gallery loads quick.-Camera kind of sucks. Its usable for quick pictures and sharing good times, but I'm not going to print them out and frame them.+Skype works!! Well it doesn't work from the phone to a computer for some reason. But it works great from phone to phone. Had a great chat with my Brother on his EVO 4g.+They send you Txt reminders for making the prepaid payment on time starting 3 days before they're due.**Wifi Calling is installed and works great but it uses your minutes. Originally I thought I would get a minutes plan to save money and use wifi calling as much as possible but no-can-do. Wifi is just a way to get you service in low service areas. It still uses your minutes, so I moved to the unl minutes plan.I will say the less apps you put on a phone the better they run. The App Market is just not as well managed as Apple's App Store. The Apps in the Market can take up excessive memory, create memory leaks that increase the memory they take up even when closed, they conflict sometimes with other apps due to the access privileges they require, they slow the phone down.I watch carefully thru a memory monitoring app and see what apps do to the phone system and delete those that cause issues.I can get 3 days out of this phone's battery this way.Fortunately, which is something I love about this phone, most of the software I use is on the phone and it works really well. I'm very happy with it.The Service:I switched from Sprint. I'm glad I did. I paid $200 for the phone and now just pay the prepaid 4g monthly of $50/mo. I get unlm talk and text and 100mb of data at 4g and then unlimited data at 2g/3g. Its good for the occasional Navigated trip and getting emails (w/o attachments). Product Name: SONY XPERIA Z3 COMPACT D5803 16GB (FACTORY UNLOCKED) INTERNATIONAL MODEL- WHITE No-Warranty
Reviews: No cyanogenmod available for it yet so the Sony-branded vibe instead of vanilla Android bothers me somewhat, but it's a fantastic upgrade from my Galaxy Nexus and a real pleasure to have flagship-level power in a compact phone. It's fast, smooth, and everything that you would expect in a new phone performance-wise.Very exciting that there is a camera button instead of having to tap the screen to take pictures (which often results in blurrier photos). I didn't test the camera in low-light conditions before unlocking the bootloader, so I can't comment on how much functionality/quality was lost there. The low-light photos I shoot now are neither impressively good or bad, just slightly grainy and slow like you would probably expect from a reasonable quality phone camera.Battery is awesome. I've been interacting with this a lot more than my old phone because it's new, and even with my constant fussing around all day, I'm only charging it once every two nights. I'm not watching movies all day or anything, but am actively customizing, installing, texting, trying out new apps, etc.The back is extremely slippery, like it was designed to be a high-performance air hockey puck. If it sits on anything with a slight incline, it starts gliding away by itself -- this includes rubberized surfaces. This is the first phone I've put a case on in the last 5 years, but this phone is small enough that I don't feel put off by a little extra bulk. That case is mostly to keep the phone from floating away on its slippery back.The notification light is in the corner and much more subtle than other phones that I have had, which could be a good or bad thing depending on your preference. I rely pretty heavily on Lightflow color notifications to silently let me know what is going on from across a room or table, so this may take some getting used to.It's kind of annoying to have to either use the wireless charging (which reviews from around the web have referenced can tear the plate out of the phone), or to have to remove the waterproof cover flap every time I need to plug in the USB cable. The flap is held on by a small piece of plastic so that it hangs off the phone during charging. I like to keep phones around for 2 years or so before upgrading, and wouldn't be too surprised if this broke during the usual life of my phones.Overall, a solid purchase that I am quite in love with, and cannot wait for stable alternative ROMs to appear!

Reviews: So far so good. I am coming from a Nexus 5 and needed an upgrade. I tried the Pixel and it was an amazing phone, loved the simplicity of Google phones but not the price. I was really worried because I have grown really fond of plain android over the last 3 years but the cyber sale was too good to pass up. When I got the phone, I was immediately turned off by the lack of an app drawer so after about 30 mins with the phone I downloaded the Google Now launcher and all was well!!! I also downloaded all of the standard google apps (gmail, photos, messanger, calander, keep, clock...) while uninstalling as much of the bloat as possible (good thing Honor comes pretty bare). I read up on the net about all of the buried settings to enable/disable apps from running in the background while off. Now the phone runs great, and I can barely tell its a not plain android, except the notification setting pull down as it takes some getting used to.This phone is very fast and has a great camera, not as good as the pixel but it was about 500$ less I think I can live with it! The fingerprint sensor is crazy fast and I love that you can set it up as a shortcut for different tasks, especially because the power and volume being on the same side of the phone made taking screenshots one handed very difficult. Now I can set my fingerprint double tap to take care of that.Time will tell if this phone holds up, I'm still concerned about the possibility of not getting security updates or OS updates but we'll see. For now I am happy about my purchase. If anyone is reading this and is on the fence, just do it!!!

Reviews: This phone is a brick!I've broken many phones over my smart phone career, but not this phone. This windows phone is really easy to use, has awesome contact integration, durable and reliable. There are lots of third party app developers that release apps that mimic big name apps(SnapChat, Tinder etc..), most of these apps allow you to connect to the actual service itself, sometimes these apps can function better than the real thing (Like the old 6-Snap, 6-Tin or 6-Tag etc...), but most of time you just want to be on the same page as everyone else using the official app. However, with Windows 10 mobile, I'm sure that will all soon change.A few months ago I switched to a Galaxy S6 Edge solely because I wanted to have mobile banking apps and Snapchat. I absolutely can't stand my new S6 edge (I have to restart my S6 Edge daily because the OS get's very glitched/slow after a short period of use), it doesn't even come close to Microsoft's careful attention to detail & functionality when developing their mobile OS. I never had any issue with lag on this phone, even after almost completely filling up my storage with photos, documents and apps.I've owned both iPhone and Android devices and this Windows Phone was the icing on the cake. I would prefer to use this phone over my Android any day of the year.There's a lot more to be said, but I would take the time and research if Windows Phone is right for you.I highly recommend this phone based off my experience and I see a bright future for all Windows Phones.To find out more, check out their website: https://www.windowsphone.com

Reviews: Just got the watch and I have to say I like it! it is slightly thick but not terrible. The only gripe I have for now is the setup to my phone. WHAT A PAIN IN THE ASS.. it will connect but then it doesnt pair. After an hour of putzing with it, I found out the best thing to do is install the software using the QR Code on the watch (very cool by the way) then pair with the phone. Unpair with the phone. Turn off the BT on the watch and the phone. Turn the BT back on on both devices then connect. Viola! it starts working. The remote camera option is cool if not a little creepy. Seems like it could be used for less than legal practices.. I will use and report back further issues.. If Any..EDIT: 1 Week review..So I have had this watch for a week and would like to update you on my findings. After trying all the features i have come to the conclusion that this is still a fun device to have. The sleep monitor, Working but always says poor nights sleep. I am assuming it uses the motion sensor for this and how much you move during the night. As i am a restless sleeper, the watch is spot on.. Connection to the phone: This is where the watch lacks. Patience is a virtue on this. It will connect and stay connected as long as you are in range of your phone. 10 or more feet in a normal setting. I have noticed any location that has metal studs or office environment, The range is 2-3 feet at best. Not a big deal since they have crammed so much into this watch that the antenna for BT couldn't be very large. If it does drop, simply touch the messages button and touch connect and it will reconnect. It will bring up all the notifications it missed while disconnected and it does do almost ALL notifications including facebook. It only will bring up contacts and messages it you choose the bluetooth option for each on the watch. IT DOES NOT SAVE ANYTHING TO THE WATCH. It has to download contacts and messages each time you choose it. Depending on your phone it can take a few seconds. Cell phone option: I didn't get a chance to ry this but i did put a SIM card in and it picked up the network fine. For those of you who cant get the browser to work, It only works with the cell service. The watch does not pull the internet from your phone. The Pedometer: Works great but does have a delay. Not a big deal since you arent staring at the watch while you walk. It will catch up. Finally the software setup.. I have tried many sotwares in the hope the watch will stay connected. I have decided the watch is to blame for the distance (not a deal breaker). Do not use the QR code on the watch as the software it installs is an old version. Simply go to the play store and search "Bluetooth Notification" and install. The best part is you don't need to turn off any security. Also it is the same software that is on the watch but with updates through the store and a newer version. Open the app and turn it on. Then simply Pair the watch.. MAKE SURE YOU INSTALL THE SOFTWARE FIRST BEFORE PAIRING! In conclusion, this watch is very comfortable on the wrist and is a little think but not terrible. My only major gripe besides the connection issues is the fact that the USB port on the watch is NOT covered. I have found myself being very careful around water (washing hands, rain etc.) the port faces your hand and is very easy to get water in there. Reviews: This phone is great. I like everything about it. I have had this phone for over a month. Wanted to make sure everything worked well and that it would hook up to my carrier. Exception is when the battery gets real low then I plug the phone in standard. I also put a silicone case (youwatch) on the back of the phone to help protect the camera and in case I drop the phone. I usually just keep the HDR in auto or turn it off for action shots. The camera is taking better pictures than my old (nice not cheap) digital camera. So now I only have one thing to carry around. The camera "quick on and take a picture" is a fun feature when the action is right now. Like when someone is skiing by and I don't have time to mess with a bunch of buttons. I could not see the screen very well out on the white glary mountain. So quick phone and quick answer features were helpful. I would definitely recommend this phone to anyone that wants a larger phone and camera in one great package.Update: Just discovered the adjustable blur feature on the selfie camera. (I think it just downloaded) It's adjusted so that no one (not even teens) have red spots on their faces, yet the picture is very clear and bright. Everyone wants to take their selfie with this camera. It is really fun to fill in my phone book with nice looking close up photos of all my friends.Took a picture of the horizon on top of a snow covered hill.
